context: Each move takes one disk from the top of a peg and places it on top of another peg. A smaller disk must always stay above any larger disk on the same peg.
description: The upper half shows the initial state. From left to right the pegs are A, B, and C. Six disks of different colors are stacked on A in order of increasing size from top to bottom. B and C are empty.

The lower half shows the goal. A and B are empty, and all six disks are on the rightmost peg C in the original order, smallest on top and largest on the bottom. The downward arrow labeled “Move all disks from A to C” summarizes the task. It does not represent moving the stack in one go.

frames.explanation: The figure defines the initial and target states. The intermediate steps, omitted here, must be a sequence of legal one-disk moves.
frames.title: Tower of Hanoi example: moving six disks from A to C

summary: Initially, six disks are stacked on A from smallest on top to largest on the bottom. Use B to move them all to C in their original order.
title: Tower of Hanoi example: moving six disks from A to C
